L1 and L2 oracle: scalameta 4.17.4 (BSD-3-Clause), the Scala parser scalafmt and Metals use, run as calibration/oracles/scalameta/ScalametaDump.java (a JVM bench instrument only): 26,219 definitions and 18,414 call pairs over 1,502 files, 0 parse failures (a scala-3 directory's file parsed as Scala 3 first, any other as Scala 2.13 with -Xsource:3 first). Tier B on the D2 precedent (JavaParser, the Kotlin PSI, luaparse): an independent syntactic parser, so L1 can be excellent and L2 at most good; the tier is a claim for review, not a harness fact. The parser is independent; the scope (a val or var only as a member, a field class parameter as written or of a case class, every def anywhere, a named given) is the dialect author's rule, written in the oracle's README, so sym_recall 1 and sym_precision 1 show the queries implement that rule, not that no other rule is reasonable.

universal-ctags 6.2.1 has no Scala parser (ctags --list-languages lists none), so the queue's ctags oracle does not exist; scip-java reads Scala only through SemanticDB, which needs each subject compiled by its sbt build (not installed here, a heavy cross-built JVM run), and is the L3/L4 oracle (LB-Q-scala-rest).

range_agreement .8042 (21,084 of 26,218) is the one metric under excellent, and it is the engine's, not the queries': tree-sitter-scala ends an indentation-delimited node (a body on the line after `=`, a Scala 3 template) at the next token, after the blank lines and indentation that follow it, and the engine's EndLine counts a node to its last byte, so such a definition ends on the next definition's line. Trimming trailing whitespace in the engine's end-line count (internal/extractor/tsextract.go tsEndLine, not this item's file) reads .9511 on the same subjects and oracle (24,937 of 26,218), which would make L1 excellent (O761).

calls cross-check, not scored: the grammar's own upstream queries/tags.scm (v0.26.2, MIT) run by py-tree-sitter 0.25.2 (calibration/oracles/ts-tags/scala-tags.scm, tier C) reads call_recall .9887 (6,808 of 6,886) but call_precision .3896, because its only call pattern is a plain f(x): a member call (xs.map(f), F.pure(a)), most of Scala's, is in no pair it writes. L2 is graded against the scalameta pairs, which read a member call.
